title: Session reports reach Tally without being asked

requirements.text: When a session told with genlock tell --do finishes a turn, Tally receives a [relay] with that reply without sending a follow-up --ask
requirements.check: genlock tell a session --do, let it finish, and check Tally's conversation log for a [relay] arriving before any further message from Tally

fields.symptom: Reports for Tally reached it only after a ~10 min hold: agent-genlock's project Assistant replied at 22:40:18 and Tally got it at 22:50:56, after TJ had already asked
fields.root_cause: relayToAssistant counted every running session owing any reply as still owing Tally, including sessions whose reply is owed to a project Assistant (awaiting-reply.json from=sub). nightmaremode's director session worked 30+ min for its own Assistant, so Tally's reports waited the full holdSeconds (600 s)
whys: The hold was written when only Tally told sessions; the from field added for Subassistants was never read by the hold
Delegation changed who owes whom, but the app's owing count kept the old single-asker model
fields.corrective: Tally is held only by replies owed to it (RelayRouting.owesTally); a project Assistant only by replies owed to it (RelayRouting.owes), read from the channel's owedTo

text: Cause found and fixed in source (Voice.swift owesTally/owes/owedTo; AppModel relayToAssistant). Live repro observed: sub relay written 22:51:09 released 23:01:18 while nightmaremode d0adbf owed its own sub. Unit tests pass, app builds. Live check needs the installed app relaunched (kills running sessions): waiting on TJ. AppModel.swift also holds another session's uncommitted grid-join edits: commit by hunk.

evidence: After installing the fixed app and relaunching it (01:52:08 UTC 14 Nov), I ran genlock tell lunenburgbudgets --do --session main with Tally's env at 01:53:03. Reply relay written 01:53:15 (ack started). Tally's transcript 3063f4c1 shows [relay] at 01:54:17.6 with no Tally message in between; Tally answered 'session replies are reaching me again'. Two sessions that owe a sub were working throughout (8515592D for B7D6E00C, 7E763BCD for 2060DD93 from 01:53:58); under the old rule either would have held the relay 600 s. The one remaining wait was nightmaremode's sub, which owed Tally directly and was mid-turn until 01:54:16.7 (intended).

answers.observed: relay written 01:53:15, at Tally 01:54:17.6 (transcript 3063f4c1); before the fix, 22:40:18 to 22:50:56 and 22:51:09 to 23:01:18
answers.cause: measured: the unfixed app released a held relay at exactly holdSeconds while d0adbf (owing its sub) worked; with the fix, working sub-owing sessions did not hold it
answers.absence: the 30 s wait was traced to a sub owing Tally directly and mid-turn (turn end 01:54:16.7), not left unexplained
answers.assumption: that the relaunched app runs the new build: installed from build at 01:51, new pid 89491; the 66 s delivery, not 600 s, with two sub-owing sessions working, is consistent only with the new rule
answers.falsify: a relay for Tally sitting about 600 s while Tally is idle and only sub-owing sessions are working
